findings.who: A filer who files married filing separately and whose spouse is on active duty in the U.S. armed forces in 2025; the filer did not serve.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about a spouse only 'on a joint return'; reading that parenthetical as limiting, the filer answers no because the return is not joint.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30: 'Special rules under the SCRA apply to members of the military and their spouses for determining residency.'
findings.fix: Remove 'on a joint return' from the gate and the gated question; ask about you or your spouse regardless of filing status, or ask separately for MFS spouses.

findings.who: A surviving spouse filing a 2025 joint return whose spouse died in 2025 while on active duty, but who did not move in 2025 under military orders after the death.
findings.why_no: The help says 'Count a spouse who has died if you moved in 2025 under military orders after the death'; read as the only case for a deceased spouse, it leads the filer to answer no.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30: 'unless you were in active service in the military'; also 'Special rules under the SCRA apply to members of the military and their spouses for determining residency.'
findings.fix: State that a deceased spouse counts if the spouse served in 2022 or later, including active duty in 2025 at death, whether or not the filer moved under orders; make the move rule a separate condition if needed.

findings.who: A member of the U.S. Space Force on active duty at some time in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate lists 'U.S. armed forces, Coast Guard, reserves or National Guard' but does not name the Space Force; a filer may read the list as the complete set and answer no.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30: 'unless you were in active service in the military.'
findings.fix: Add 'Space Force' or say 'any branch or component of the U.S. armed forces, including the Space Force, Coast Guard, reserves, and National Guard.'

findings.who: A filer who is currently on active duty in 2025 and has been serving continuously since before 2022.
findings.why_no: The gate asks 'In 2022 or later, did you serve' in the past tense; the filer may read it as asking about completed service and answer no because they are still serving, not a veteran.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30: 'unless you were in active service in the military.'
findings.fix: Use present-perfect or current-service wording: 'At any time since January 1, 2022, including currently, have you or your spouse served or been on active duty...?'
